3) Follow up with a short technical deep-dive (30 min) for your infra/engineering team to walk through streaming traces and tuning knobs.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: ACME Health — post-demo recap & next steps

Sam — thanks, see the initial model-fit recommendations and artifacts attached. High-level summary first: 

- Recommended models (to evaluate in order):
  1) "Redwood-Realtime-7B-Quant" (optimized for streaming; best balance of latency + partial coherence).
  2) "Llama2-13B-Q4_P" (good quality; slightly higher p99 latency but stronger final-output coherence).
  3) "Redwood-Completion-70B-Int8" (for batch/long-form postprocessing where latency is less critical).

- Suggested configs for streaming eval (start with these):
  * max_new_tokens: 256
  * stop_sequences: ["\n\n\n", "<END_NOTE>"]
  * temperature: 0.2
  * streaming_chunk_size: 64 tokens (tune down if you see partial incoherence at chunk boundaries)
  * prefix_caching: enabled for repeated patient/system prompts

- Latency expectations (based on our benchmarks at similar throughput):
  * Redwood-Realtime-7B-Quant — median token latency ~12ms, request turnaround (median) ~180ms for 120-token outputs under continuous streaming with batching.
  * Llama2-13B-Q4_P — p50 ~260ms, p95 ~1s (depends on batch size), better final-token coherence.

Attached: redwood-model-recommendations.pdf (detailed model tradeoffs), acme-prompt-sets.csv (2k prompt subset to reproduce), benchmark-summary.txt (linked metrics and test harness).

Notes on stop sequences: we recommend normalizing incoming transcripts so stop markers are consistent (we included a mapping in the CSV). If you see truncation, try the lower temperature + increase streaming_chunk_size slightly or migrate to single-chunk response for the final token bracket.

Next steps:
- I can run the evaluation against the attached prompt set this week and share detailed traces.
- Jordan (cc) will follow up with a short note on streaming traces/UX issues we saw in your sample.

I'll book the deep-dive for Wed 17 Jun 11:00am PT unless you prefer a different slot (you mentioned Wed 10-11am PT).

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme-health.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 07:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME Health — streaming UX notes (partial output coherence)

Sam / team — quick technical note from the eval traces Marissa sent. I ran the first pass across the prompt subset and flagged a few repeatable UX patterns: 

1) Partial-output incoherence at chunk boundaries: when streaming_chunk_size is small (<=32) and the model outputs long nested lists, we saw mid-stream token drift. Workarounds: increase chunk_size to 64 or enable small lookahead buffering (we can provide a patch for the streaming client).

2) Premature stop triggers: we observed the model treating some bracketed clinical shorthand as stop signals. Recommend normalizing the transcript and adding a short guard token (e.g., "<CONTINUE>") to your ingestion pipeline so the model doesn't prematurely hit stop_sequences.

3) Latency spikes correlated with on-the-fly quantized kernel swaps under burst load. If you pick Redwood-Realtime-7B-Quant, enable the dedicated warm pool option (we can quote this) or use a slightly larger batch target to smooth p95.

Attached is a short trace file (streaming-traces-ACME-1234.log) and a link with per-request IDs so you can cross-reference the HubSpot tickets. Proposed immediate next steps:
- Marissa to share final eval report (today).
- Dev / ACME infra to try the normalized stop token + chunk_size=64 config on a small canary set.
- Schedule 30-min deep-dive to review streaming traces (Marissa to confirm Wed 11am PT).

If you want, I can also pair with your engs during the canary run to look at live traces.

—Jordan
Product Lead, Inference | Redwood Inference
